stories.body: President Donald Trump threatened the European Union with potentially severe tariffs or a halt in trade if it proceeds with a proposal to make Canada its first associate member. The proposal, advanced as Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks to reduce Canada's dependence on the United States, would deepen cooperation on technology, defence and energy but still requires approval from all 27 EU member states. European officials said the initiative was not directed against Washington and that the United States has no authority to dictate Europe's political or geopolitical choices. Canada has also formally applied to join the British-led Joint Expeditionary Force, underscoring its effort to diversify defence relationships.
stories.headline: Trump threatens EU tariffs over proposed Canada associate membership

stories.body: The United States has again denied Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas a visa to attend the UN General Assembly in New York, extending visa sanctions against Palestinian Authority and Palestine Liberation Organization officials for a second consecutive year. The State Department accused Palestinian leaders of failing to meet peace-process commitments, pursuing statehood recognition through international bodies and glorifying terrorism; Palestinian officials rejected the move as unjustified and contrary to efforts to rebuild relations and pursue a two-state solution. The decision renews questions over US obligations under the UN Headquarters Agreement, although the Palestinian UN mission's regular staff retain a waiver and the General Assembly is expected to consider allowing Abbas to address it by video.
stories.headline: US again denies Palestinian leaders visas for the UN General Assembly

stories.body: A war-damaged residential building sheltering displaced Palestinian families collapsed in Gaza City, killing at least 21 people, including children, and injuring at least 25 others. Rescuers said people remained trapped beneath the rubble and that the recovery effort was hampered by a lack of heavy equipment, leaving some workers digging by hand. The building had previously been struck during the war and was structurally weakened; its collapse also hit tents beside it. The disaster highlights the danger facing Palestinians living in thousands of damaged buildings amid a shortage of safe shelter and restrictions on reconstruction equipment.
stories.headline: At least 21 killed as a damaged building collapses in Gaza City

stories.body: Ukraine said Russia struck a Tanzanian-flagged civilian ship in the Black Sea, killing its captain, as loud overnight explosions were reported in Kyiv and authorities issued a missile alert for the capital. The reported strike and attacks come as Ukraine continues to face Russian pressure on both its maritime routes and major cities.
stories.headline: Ukraine says Russia struck a civilian ship in the Black Sea as explosions hit Kyiv

stories.body: Israel and Morocco agreed to upgrade their diplomatic missions to full embassies and appoint ambassadors after talks between their foreign ministers in New York hosted by the US ambassador to the United Nations. The countries also plan to expand air travel, restore direct flights and complete agreements on investment protection and double taxation by the end of the year. Morocco and Israel established diplomatic relations in 2020 under the US-brokered Abraham Accords, and the announcement came one day after the accords' sixth anniversary.
stories.headline: Israel and Morocco agree to open embassies, upgrading relations under the Abraham Accords

stories.body: Turkish authorities have carried out a broad crackdown on LGBTQ+ organisations, HIV-advocacy groups, journalists and protesters, using allegations of obscenity and related offences. Police raided offices, homes and venues in several cities, while rights groups said at least 62 people were being held on remand and more than 100 had been detained; further arrests followed protests in Istanbul, Ankara and İzmir. Turkey's justice minister said the operation was intended to protect children, families and social order, but Human Rights Watch and local organisations described it as the country's widest recent crackdown on LGBTQ+ people. Same-sex relations are legal in Turkey, though the government has intensified restrictions on LGBTQ+ activity in recent years.
stories.headline: Turkey detains dozens in crackdown on LGBTQ+ activists and journalists

stories.body: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest-rate range by a quarter percentage point to 3.75% to 4%, its first increase in more than three years, saying inflation has remained too high for too long. Chair Kevin Warsh described the unanimous decision as sober and responsible, arguing that a strong labour market and economy allowed the central bank to keep its focus on price stability. President Donald Trump, who had publicly demanded rapid rate cuts, said he supported Warsh but criticized the Fed board as hostile and political. Higher rates raise borrowing costs for mortgages, consumer credit and business loans while potentially improving returns on savings.
stories.headline: Federal Reserve raises interest rates for the first time in three years, defying Trump's calls for cuts

stories.body: A federal judge warned that the Trump administration's intensified immigration enforcement in Minnesota threatened democratic norms. The broader ICE crackdown has continued to rely on cooperation with local law-enforcement agencies, with hundreds of undocumented immigrants recently arrested in a five-day operation in Indiana.
stories.headline: Judge warns Trump's immigration surge in Minnesota threatened democracy

stories.body: Spain's National Court has temporarily halted plans to install a 16,000-square-metre migrant camp at the port of Ceuta, which was intended to house roughly 1,000 people after a mass arrival at the end of July. The court acted on an emergency appeal by the Unified Police Union, which argued that the government had not properly published or notified its order and that safety, emergency and occupational-risk conditions had not been demonstrated for a critical port facility. The Transport Ministry has been ordered to submit the relevant administrative file, while the government said the suspension blocked an imminent humanitarian operation that could accommodate up to 1,700 people.
stories.headline: Spain's National Court halts a migrant camp planned for Ceuta's port

stories.body: National Court judge María Tardón has expanded the investigation into the mass arrival of migrants in Ceuta on July 30 and 31, seeking to identify who organised, financed and coordinated the movement of tens of thousands of people toward the border. She has requested assistance from police and Spain's intelligence service to identify alleged on-the-ground facilitators through facial-recognition and international databases, and has sought records from major technology platforms to trace accounts, phone numbers, connections and messages used to spread the call to gather. The judge has also summoned Ceuta's president and a former senior government-delegation aide as witnesses and requested risk warnings issued before the event.
stories.headline: Spain investigates the circumstances behind the mass migrant arrival in Ceuta

stories.body: Spain's Congress rejected the government's emergency decree regulating lobbying, ending a measure that had been in force for less than a month and would have created a mandatory public register of interest groups. The proposal fell by 179 votes to 155, with 12 abstentions, after opposition from the PP, Vox, Junts and UPN and abstentions among several smaller parties. While many parties backed the principle of greater lobbying transparency, they criticized the use of an emergency decree and the treatment of employers' associations and trade unions as lobbyists. The failure is expected to cost Spain about €260 million in EU recovery funds tied to the reform.
stories.headline: Spain's Congress rejects the government's lobbying law

stories.body: Heavy overnight rain continued to disrupt transport across Barcelona and the surrounding area, leaving the L4 metro operating only between La Pau and Verdaguer and the L11 with limited service. A new sinkhole or washout near Montcada i Reixac halted R2, R2 Nord and R11 commuter trains between Sant Andreu and Granollers Centre, while other rail services ran with delays or speed restrictions. At least 20 flights were cancelled at Barcelona airport, flooding affected hospital basements and rail facilities, and firefighters responded to 158 incidents including inundations, fallen trees and electrical problems. About 700 electricity customers remained without power, largely in Nou Barris, Horta-Guinardó and Sant Andreu.
stories.headline: Torrential rain disrupts transport across Barcelona and damages infrastructure

stories.body: Catalonia's interior minister, Núria Parlon, defended the timing of ES-Alert emergency messages sent during Wednesday night's severe rain, saying they were issued when residents needed to protect themselves rather than simply because it was raining heavily. Officials said the first alert was sent around 9:30 p.m., after Meteocat raised the danger level to the maximum 6 out of 6 in Barcelona and the Maresme, and a later alert covered additional districts as the storms advanced. Parlon and civil-protection officials said they could issue warnings preventively when extreme risk is forecast in advance, but warned that indiscriminate alerts would reduce public trust. They also said the Barcelona football match underway at Camp Nou did not require suspension, though the alert was intended in part to influence how supporters travelled afterward.
stories.headline: Barcelona officials defend the timing of emergency alerts during the storm

stories.body: Barcelona City Council has opposed a possible drinking-water treatment plant on La Ponderosa, the city's last agricultural estate, after it emerged that Aigües de Barcelona acquired its more than nine hectares in 2024. Deputy mayor Laia Bonet said the city supports water infrastructure that improves metropolitan resilience to drought but argued that La Ponderosa is not an appropriate location and that alternative sites have been proposed. The council wants the land protected as agricultural space and incorporated into the Agrovallbona project, which aims to support agroecology, training, research and opportunities for the Vallbona neighbourhood.
stories.headline: Barcelona rejects plans for a water-treatment plant on the city's last agricultural estate
